title: A celebration with room for less
meaning: Creating beauty together can delight you, while the pursuit of abundance may obscure the simple pleasure of being close.
text: A lovely table, music and something delicious can become your way of inviting each other to relax. In the physical position of Svadhisthana, the Empress appears through these tangible preparations: you make something the two of you can enjoy. In energy, the same Empress describes a more vulnerable wish to fill the evening to the brim, as though a small pleasure could never be enough. The Lovers in emotions let you feel what matters within that lovely setting: mutual attraction and the delight of turning towards each other.

Imagine an evening spent baking a pie together. There is pastry on your fingers, some filling has escaped, and tasting the warm edge makes you laugh. **The celebration becomes shared when you notice each other.** Enjoyment is already happening, although you have yet to lay the table. That laughter and the piece you share can become the memory, alongside the beautiful finished pie you eventually set before yourselves.

Things become harder when pleasure constantly needs another addition: one more dish, another purchase, a prettier table. You keep preparing an experience and meet each other within it less often. Even thoughtful suggestions can begin to sound like demands for greater delight. Attraction then gives way to waiting for a grateful response, and enjoyment becomes the work of maintaining a celebration that never quite begins.
